title: Values and loops in Swift
summary: Use an array, a filtered loop, and an explicit return type to count positives.

scenario.briefing: A campus app summarizes stock changes. Count positive changes in Swift without hiding the result type.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

misconceptions.description: Using ! without evidence that a value exists.
misconceptions.feedback: Force unwrapping traps on nil. Use if let or guard let.
let is immutable. Use var for a value that changes.

sections.title: Swift values and decisions
sections.body: Swift declares constants with let count = 3 and variables with var total = 0. Type inference keeps the declaration concise. An optional Int? either contains an Int or nil. if let, guard let, and optional chaining make absence explicit. if and switch select branches, and switch must be exhaustive. A for loop visits a collection: for value in values { ... }.
